title: Honey and Thyme Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Honey replaces the sugar and fresh thyme is infused instead of vanilla; four yolks.
summary: Our classic French custard with honey in place of sugar and fresh thyme infused in the dairy instead of vanilla. Floral, gently herby and lovely with fruit.

ingredients.note: strained out; nutrition counts a little

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Infuse
steps.text: Bring the milk, cream and thyme to the boil, then cover and leave off the heat for 20 min. Strain and pour the dairy back into the pan.

steps.title: Whisk the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks in the heatproof bowl.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Whisk in about 250 ml of the warm dairy a little at a time, then the honey, then the rest of the dairy.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Return to the pan and stir over low heat until the custard reaches 77-80 °C and coats the spatula. Do not let it simmer.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Stir in the salt, strain, cool in the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn, then freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: A mild floral honey lets the thyme come through; strong dark honey dominates.
A common mistake is adding honey straight to the yolks, which can make them seize. Add some warm dairy first.
Lemon thyme works beautifully here too.
storage: Freeze in a covered container for up to 2 weeks. Honey keeps it a little softer than sugar does.
